Hoppin' John

Served at: New Year's Day

Serves 6-8Prep 20 min (plus optional overnight soak)Cook 1 hour 30 min

Hoppin' John is a traditional Southern dish made with black-eyed peas and rice, often served with collard greens and cornbread. It is a staple on New Year's Day, believed to bring good luck and prosperity for the coming year, with the peas symbolizing coins and the greens representing paper money.

Ingredients

  • 1 pound (450g) dried black-eyed peas
  • 6 cups (1.4 L) chicken or vegetable broth
  • 1 tablespoon (15ml) olive oil or bacon fat
  • 4 ounces (113g) smoked ham hock, bacon, or salt pork, diced
  • 1 large yellow onion, chopped
  • 1 green bell pepper, chopped
  • 2 celery stalks, chopped
  • 3 cloves garlic, minced
  • 1 teaspoon dried thyme
  • 1/2 teaspoon smoked paprika
  • 1/4 teaspoon cayenne pepper (optional)
  • 1 bay leaf
  • 1 1/2 cups (300g) long-grain white rice
  • Salt and freshly ground black pepper to taste
  • Fresh parsley or green onions, chopped, for garnish

Method

  1. Rinse the dried black-eyed peas thoroughly. For quicker cooking, soak them in cold water overnight, then drain. Alternatively, use the quick-soak method: cover peas with water, bring to a boil for 10 minutes, then remove from heat and let stand for 1 hour, then drain.
  2. In a large Dutch oven or heavy-bottomed pot, heat the olive oil or bacon fat over medium heat. Add the diced ham hock, bacon, or salt pork and cook until crispy, about 5-7 minutes. Remove the meat with a slotted spoon and set aside, leaving the rendered fat in the pot.
  3. Add the chopped onion, green bell pepper, and celery to the pot. Sauté until softened, about 8-10 minutes.
  4. Stir in the minced garlic, dried thyme, smoked paprika, and cayenne pepper (if using). Cook for 1 minute until fragrant.
  5. Add the drained black-eyed peas, chicken or vegetable broth, and bay leaf to the pot. Bring to a boil, then reduce heat to low, cover, and simmer for 45-60 minutes, or until the peas are tender but not mushy. Stir occasionally.
  6. Once the peas are tender, stir in the long-grain white rice and the reserved cooked meat (if using bacon or salt pork, ham hock can remain in the pot). Bring the mixture back to a gentle simmer.
  7. Cover the pot and continue to cook for another 15-20 minutes, or until the rice is tender and has absorbed most of the liquid. If the mixture becomes too dry before the rice is cooked, add a little more broth or water.
  8. Remove the bay leaf. Season with salt and freshly ground black pepper to taste. Let it rest, covered, for 5 minutes before serving.
  9. Garnish with fresh parsley or chopped green onions before serving hot.

Tips

  • For a vegetarian version, omit the ham hock/bacon and use vegetable broth. A dash of liquid smoke can add a smoky flavor.
  • Serve Hoppin' John with a side of collard greens (for 'money') and cornbread (for 'gold') to complete the traditional New Year's Day meal.
  • Leftovers are said to be 'Skippin' Jenny' and are considered even luckier the next day.
